title: The Winter of Old Chapel Road
premise: Sable Delacroix arrives in the dying town of Hollowmere to teach at Old Chapel School, where eleven students have vanished over sixty years and the town keeps meticulous, complicit records. When an excavation crew unearths a door beneath the schoolhouse — sealed from the inside — Sable discovers her own family helped build whatever waits behind it, and that the missing children were never missing at all. As the count of taken souls approaches its terrible completion, Sable must lead the last endangered family out through the dark beneath the chapel, confronting the ancestor who made the bargain and choosing to break it at the cost of her own name. The door is closed forever, but only because someone stays behind to hold it shut.
about_author: Ulyana Quintana is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in one-room schoolhouses across the northern plains before turning to horror full-time. She writes about institutions, ledgers, and the quiet violence of small towns that keep their promises too well.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Sable Delacroix's POV. She arrives in Hollowmere on the first frost, takes roll in a classroom with three empty desks no one will explain, and begins her documentation habit — every anomaly written down like a prayer. Emotional beat: wary hope curdling into unease as the principal, Mr. Voss, corrects her roster by removing a name she swears she read aloud.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cleaning the supply closet, she finds a leather ledger dating to 1897 listing students under two columns: Present and Held. Every child marked Held has a date but no return date. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the intoxicating thrill of discovery; she photographs every page, telling herself it's for the school board.

chapters.title: The Wren Family
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Sable and Odile Wren, mother of her student Cass. Odile is warm, exhausted, and evasive about why the family never leaves town despite obvious poverty. Cass draws the same door over and over. Emotional beat: tenderness establishing stakes — this family, these children, are who Sable will fight for.

chapters.title: Excavation Day
chapters.summary: Crew foreman Denny Kowalczyk's POV. The state-mandated foundation repair crew breaks ground behind the schoolhouse and strikes not stone but iron — a door, hinges on the inside, sealed from within. The radio dies. One worker, Petey, hears his dead brother calling his name from below. Emotional beat: blue-collar bravado collapsing into animal fear.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She reaches the pit as the crowd gathers; the door is warm, and frost forms around it in summer patterns. In the ledger's final page she finds today's date pre-written beside the word Count. Emotional beat: vertigo — her documentation habit becomes evidence that something has been documenting her.

chapters.title: What the Town Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the historical society, Odile quietly burns a box of papers and warns Sable to stop asking about the Held column. We learn the founding families — Delacroix among them — traded the door a tithe of children in exchange for the town never freezing, never starving. Emotional beat: shame and complicity; justice outside the law begins here, in what was never legal to begin with.

chapters.title: Petey Answers
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Petey, sleepless since excavation day, walks into the pit at 3 a.m. and knocks. The door opens inward onto darkness and he steps through; the crew finds only his boots, placed neatly. The count ledger updates itself in Sable's classroom copy. Emotional beat: grief weaponized — the thing below knows exactly which voices we cannot refuse.

chapters.title: The Delacroix Clause
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Researching her own surname, she learns her great-grandmother signed the original covenant and that each generation produces one Keeper — a Delacroix who hears the count. Sable has been hearing numbers in her sleep all week. Emotional beat: identity crisis; inheritance as sentence rather than gift.

chapters.title: Twenty-Three
chapters.summary: Cass Wren's POV, first child perspective. Cass counts aloud in class without meaning to, and the other children go silent when she reaches twenty-three — the number needed to complete the count. That night frost writes names on the Wrens' windows. Emotional beat: childhood innocence turned instrument; the horror of being chosen before you can consent.

chapters.title: Voss Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She confronts Principal Voss with the ledger; he neither denies nor confirms, only says the town tried ending it in 1954 and lost fourteen people in one winter. The law won't help — no crime has technically occurred. Emotional beat: institutional betrayal; the realization that official channels are part of the mechanism.

chapters.title: The Road Out Is Closed
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile tries to flee with Cass and her son Bram; the highway loops them back to Hollowmere no matter which direction they drive, gas gauge unmoved. The town isn't trapping them — the covenant is. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair; escape must happen downward, not outward.

chapters.title: Denny's Confession
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Drunk and ruined, Denny admits to Sable that his crew's contract came from a shell company registered to the Delacroix estate — she was summoned, engineered, delivered. He also reveals the door hums louder each night. Emotional beat: rage transmuting into resolve; Sable stops being prey and starts planning.

chapters.title: The Undercroft Map
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following her great-grandmother's marginalia in the parish bible, Sable maps the tunnels beneath the chapel — old smuggler routes that bypass the sealed door entirely. The map requires blood-ink to stay legible. Emotional beat: grim competence; the prayer of documentation finally becoming actionable.

chapters.title: Bram Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Bram begins sleepwalking toward the schoolhouse each night, speaking in a chorus voice, counting down from twenty-three. Odile ties him to the bed and hates herself for it. Emotional beat: maternal terror at its rawest; the clock is now audible in a child's mouth.

chapters.title: The Congregation of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, dream sequence bleeding into waking. Through the keyhole Sable sees the Held children — decades of them, unaged, arranged in rows, kept rather than killed, waiting for the count to complete so they can be released or consumed. Her great-grandmother stands among them, still signing. Emotional beat: horrified pity; the enemy is also a prison.

chapters.title: Breaking the Quorum
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The town meets in the chapel; Voss argues completion brings peace, half the town agrees out of exhaustion. Sable publicly reads the Held ledger aloud, forcing the town to hear sixty years of names. Emotional beat: the climax of the justice theme — testimony as resistance when courts don't exist.

chapters.title: Down Through the Smugglers' Dark
chapters.summary: Sable, Odile, Denny, and the Wren children enter the undercroft as the count hits twenty-two. Tunnels narrow; the chorus voice offers each of them their deepest grief as payment to turn back. Denny nearly takes the deal for Petey. Emotional beat: descent both literal and moral; everyone's price named aloud.

chapters.title: The Door From the Other Side
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They reach the door's inner face and find it can only be resealed by a Keeper — a Delacroix — standing on the inside. Her great-grandmother's ghost explains the covenant's loophole: the count completes only if the Keeper consents. Sable realizes what breaking it costs. Emotional beat: the trap's true shape revealed; sacrifice framed as choice, not fate.

chapters.title: The Count Reaches Twenty-Three
chapters.summary: Odile's POV above ground as the town, desperate and half-mad, delivers Cass to the pit — the twenty-third. Below, Sable feels the count land in her bones. She refuses consent, and the covenant, denied its Keeper's yes, begins to collapse, taking the held children with it unless they run now. Emotional beat: peak terror and fury; the system demands we vote for our own consumption.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, climax. Sable sends the freed children up through the tunnels while she holds the failing door shut from within, renaming herself out of the Delacroix line — 'I am no one's inheritance' — which severs the covenant's claim. The door seals with her on the wrong side. Emotional beat: triumphant tragedy; identity destroyed and self-authored in the same breath.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, aftermath. The children surface; the frost recedes; Hollowmere wakes to a spring it doesn't remember how to deserve. The ledger's Held column is blank. Odile drives the Wren family out on an open road and does not look back. Emotional beat: grief braided with release; survival as an obligation to the remembered.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Sable's POV from beyond the door. In the dark, she keeps writing — a new ledger, names of the freed, dates of their safe arrivals — and somewhere above, teachers in distant towns find pages they didn't write. The last line: the count is zero, and holding. Emotional beat: quiet, uncanny grace; the prayer continues, answered.
